title: Model scouting opportunity matrix and competitive metrics
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a prioritized opportunity matrix and tracking cadence for new open and closed-source models that matter to Redwood customers. Deliverables: 1) Opportunity matrix with scoring across performance, cost, infra fit, privacy/regulatory fit, partner potential; 2) A lightweight weekly tracking dashboard (source list + signal taxonomy) for signals we care about; 3) Recommendations for 3 pilot integrations (compatibility + commercial approach). This ticket coordinates PM research, a short engineering feasibility review, and a design touchpoint for dashboard mockups.
background: Competitive landscape is evolving faster than our current model watchlist cadence. Recent customer asks (enterprise legal+finance) emphasize latency and quantization readiness; growth teams care about model cost per token and licensing. Existing artifacts (PM-5098 rubric and market-scan docs) are high-level; this task produces an operational matrix we can action on with engineering and BD.
goals: Operationalize model scouting so product/eng/BD can prioritize integrations within two weeks
Produce a repeatable scoring rubric used by PM and Research
Identify 3 high-impact pilots (one hosted, one dedicated capacity optimization, one private deployment use case)
acceptance_criteria: Opportunity matrix completed with 12 candidate models and scores populated
Scoring rubric documented and agreed by Eng/Research/BD (sign-off message in ticket)
Tracking spreadsheet + weekly ingestion list created and a mocked dashboard in Figma linked
3 pilot recommendations with rough feasibility notes and estimated engineering effort
tasks: Assemble candidate model list (sources: Hugging Face trending, academic preprints, vendor announcements, GitHub stars)
Draft scoring rubric and weights (quality, latency, quantization-readiness, license risk, integration effort, strategic partner potential)
Run quickbench (existing infra) for top-6 models to capture latency/cost baselines (ENG help)
Interview 3 enterprise customers about model constraints (legal/compliance, on-prem requirements)
Create Figma dashboard mockups and a Google Sheet scoring matrix
score_rubric: Quality: 0-10 (based on perf on Redwood evals / public benchmarks)
Latency / Inference cost: 0-10 (measured on our default runtime/quantization)
Quantization readiness: 0-5 (binary + graded for known compatible formats)
Integration effort: 0-5 (API changes, custom kernels, tokenizer differences)
Partner potential: 0-5 (likelihood of joint go-to-market or reseller)
research_findings: Initial candidate pool (12): Llama-3 variants (community forks), Mistral-Instruct-Base, Gemma-2, RedPajama-3, Falcon-180B fine-tuned variants, OpenAssistant derivatives, MosaicML models, private vendor models with closed licensing.
Early bench notes: Mistral variants show strong quality/cost tradeoff at 8k context; Llama-3 variants require kernel tuning for NVidia 4xx GPUs, impacting integration effort.
License risks: Two community forks with unclear commercial terms flagged by Legal (link in attachments).
Enterprise signals: Finance/Analytics teams prioritize deterministic latency and KMS/HSM compatibility for private deployment pilots.
Market signals: 3 new vendor model announcements scheduled in Q2; one includes preferential OEM pricing for partners (high partner potential).
recommended_next_steps: Finalize scoring weights in 48 hours with Eng/Research (name: Connor Huang will lead feasibility checks)
Kick off quickbench jobs for top-6 models (ENG-4122) and attach results to this ticket
Schedule 30-min customer interviews and synthesize constraints in the sheet
Produce Figma dashboard and share for Design review (Evelyn Park)
Prepare a short BD outreach plan for 2 partner candidates after scoring is finalized
